card.title: Law of Mass Action and Equilibrium Constant

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The law of mass action converts equilibrium's rate-tie into a fraction. **Active mass** is molar concentration — except for pure solids and liquids, whose constant active masses (unity) banish them from every expression. Stated, the law says rate ∝ product of active masses raised to their coefficients; applied to aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, the tie k_f[A]^a[B]^b = k_r[C]^c[D]^d rearranges to **Kc = [C]^c[D]^d/[A]^a[B]^b =…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - rate = k[A]^a[B]^b - Kc = [C]^c[D]^d / [A]^a[B]^b = k_f/k_r - N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃: Kc = [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³) - CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g): Kc = [CO₂] - Units of Kc = (mol/L)^Δn

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ All cells look the same under a microscope. ✅ Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have them.  ·  ❌ DNA and RNA are identical in structure. ✅ DNA is double-stranded with deoxyribose and thymine; RNA is single-stranded with ribose and uracil.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The Haber expression*** — [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³) printed on every fertiliser-plant flow sheet: the whole ammonia industry optimises against one fraction.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Mitosis produces genetically different cells. ✅ Mitosis produces genetically identical diploid daughter cells.  ·  ❌ Meiosis produces identical cells. ✅ Meiosis produces 4 genetically diverse haploid gametes.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Expression recipe: "products up, reactants down, coefficients as powers, solids out". Flip/scale rules: reverse 1/Kc, double Kc², halve √Kc. Units: (mol/L)^Δn.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): State the law of mass action. Derive the expression for the equilibrium constant Kc for the general reaction aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD.** — **Statement:** at constant temperature, the rate of a chemical reaction is directly proportional to the product of the active masses (molar concentrations) of the reactants, each raised to…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Write the equilibrium constant expression and units for (a) N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) and (b) CaCO₃(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO₂(g).** — **(a)** Kc = [NH₃]² / ([N₂][H₂]³) — each coefficient becomes a power. Δn = (moles gaseous products) − (moles gaseous reactants) = 2 − 4 = −2, so the units are (mol/L)⁻², i.e. L²/mol².…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: In derivations, define active mass before using it and show the rate-equality step explicitly — the algebra from rates to Kc is where the marks live.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The law of mass action is Le Chatelier's quantitative root: adding reactant raises the denominator, unbalancing the fraction, and the reaction must shift forward to restore Kc — concentration effects are arithmetic, not mystery.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Active mass = molar concentration; solids/pure liquids = constant (omitted). Law of mass action: rate proportional to product of active masses raised to coefficients. Derivation: k_f[A]^a[B]^b = k_r[C]^c[D]^d → Kc = k_f/k_r = [C]^c[D]^d/[A]^a[B]^b. Kc depends only on temperature; catalyst no effect.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Blood's oxygen loading obeys mass action: more O₂ partial pressure (deep breathing) pushes haemoglobin toward the loaded form — the law written in physiology.

rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): The equilibrium constant for H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) is 49 at 450 °C. Calculate Kc for (a) 2HI ⇌ H₂ + I₂ and (b) ½H₂ + ½I₂ ⇌ HI at the same temperature.** — **(a)** Reversing an equation inverts its equilibrium constant: Kc = 1/49 ≈ **0.0204**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Law Behind Every Equilibrium Constant Guldberg and Waage (1864) turned the rate-tie of equilibrium into algebra: at equilibrium, the product of the products' concentrations divided by the product of the reactants' concentrations is a **constant** at fixed temperature.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Active mass - **Active mass = molar concentration** (mol/L), symbolised [A]; for dilute solutions and gases it is proportional to the number of moles per litre. - Active masses of **pure solids and pure liquids are constant** (taken as unity) — they never appear in equilibrium expressions; only gases and solutes do.…  ·  ## 3. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Crossing over occurs in mitosis. ✅ Crossing over occurs in Prophase I of meiosis only.  ·  ❌ All enzymes are proteins. ✅ Most enzymes are proteins; some RNA molecules (ribozymes) also have catalytic activity.  ·  ❌ ATP is the only energy currency. ✅ GTP, UTP, and CTP also serve as energy carriers in specific pathways.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Photosynthesis occurs in all plant cells. ✅ Photosynthesis occurs only in cells containing chloroplasts (mainly mesophyll).  ·  ❌ Respiration and photosynthesis are opposite processes with same equation. ✅ They are complementary but occur in different organelles and under different conditions.  ·  ❌ Oxygen is produced during respiration. ✅ Oxygen is consumed in aerobic respiration; produced during photosynthesis.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Food chain shows all feeding relationships. ✅ Food chain is linear; food web shows interconnected feeding relationships.  ·  ❌ 90% of energy is transferred to next trophic level. ✅ Only ~10% energy transfers; ~90% lost as heat.  ·  ❌ Biomagnification decreases toxin concentration up the food chain. ✅ Biomagnification increases toxin concentration at higher trophic levels.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Carbon cycle only involves plants and animals. ✅ Carbon cycle involves atmosphere, oceans, fossils, rocks, and decomposers.  ·  ❌ Nitrogen fixation only occurs in bacteria. ✅ Some lightning and industrial processes (Haber) also fix nitrogen.  ·  ❌ All fungi are harmful. ✅ Many fungi are beneficial (decomposers, mycorrhizae, food, antibiotics like penicillin).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Viruses are living organisms. ✅ Viruses are acellular — they cannot reproduce without a host and lack metabolism.  ·  ❌ Bacteria are always harmful. ✅ Most bacteria are harmless or beneficial (gut flora, nitrogen fixation, decomposition).  ·  ❌ Gram-positive and Gram-negative differ only in color. ✅ Gram-positive has thick peptidoglycan layer; Gram-negative has thin layer + outer membrane.
